title: A. G. Leventis Gallery: Masterpieces
subtitle: From an almost empty sea to a garden dense with lines, twenty works test what painters leave in and leave out.
introduction:
A sunrise can be made from a horizon, a reflection and small differences of colour. A garden may need so many intersecting marks that its trellis becomes difficult to distinguish from its growth. Both approaches appear in this selection from the A. G. Leventis Gallery, alongside rooms, portraits and urban views.

The range offers a useful way into the collection. Instead of separating every work by nationality or period, compare how much information each picture gives. A few lines can explain a rider; a crowded interior can distinguish the movements of several people. What matters is the relation between the marks and the particular subject they need to carry.

selectionNote: Artline selected these works from documented museum holdings. The selection is independent of the museum, and individual works may be on loan or off display. Dates and attributions retain the qualifications in the linked records.

works.title: Daughters of God
works.credit: Loukia Nicolaides-Vassiliou; A. G. Leventis Gallery. Source frame preserved; proportionally resized and JPEG compressed.
works.license: No reuse licence verified
works.description: The gallery identifies the women as a friend of the artist and her dressmaker. Their proximity therefore contains a difference of social position as well as pose. One leans into a supporting hand; the other turns toward her companion. Clothing and directed attention distinguish the two within a tightly joined group, giving the apparently simple pairing a specific social setting.

works.title: The Seine at Jeufosse near Vernon
works.catalogueTitle: The Seine at Jeufosse near Vernon / La Seine à Jeufosse près de Vernon
works.credit: Image source: A. G. Leventis Gallery. No item-specific reuse licence stated on museum object page
works.license: No item-specific reuse licence stated on museum object page
works.description: The curve of the bank gives the view its depth, while related touches of colour connect water, trees and reflections. Monet makes those surfaces distinguishable without assigning each a wholly separate kind of mark. Blue and violet enter the river among greens. Following their recurrence is more revealing than treating the landscape as a collection of outlined objects.

works.title: Harmony
works.medium: Oil on canvas mounted on wood
works.credit: Image source: A. G. Leventis Gallery. No item-specific reuse licence stated on museum object page
works.license: No item-specific reuse licence stated on museum object page
works.description: The orange circle encloses the profile almost like a medallion. Within it, a pale face and neck separate dark clothing from the bright ground, while the lyre identifies music. Gyzis gives the abstract title a compact visual arrangement. The image depends on the balance of a few large shapes rather than on an elaborate setting for the figure.

works.title: Composition
works.medium: Egg tempera and oil on hardboard
works.credit: Image source: A. G. Leventis Gallery. No item-specific reuse licence stated on museum object page
works.license: No item-specific reuse licence stated on museum object page
works.description: The reaching arms bridge a space otherwise divided by chairs, straight edges and contrasting clothes. Moralis makes connection a matter of geometry as well as gesture. The pale figure and the dark one retain their separate colour areas even where their bodies approach. That division gives the joined arms a clear task within the composition.

works.title: Trellises and Shadows
works.credit: Image source: A. G. Leventis Gallery. No item-specific reuse licence stated on museum object page
works.license: No item-specific reuse licence stated on museum object page
works.description: A trellis supplies a regular structure for irregular growth, but Ghikas lets the two become entangled. Poles, branches and shadows compete in a crowded field of marks. A line may initially seem architectural, then lead into foliage. The garden is held together by this mixture of construction and proliferation, with little empty space to settle their boundaries.

works.title: Tremetiousia
works.credit: George Pol. Georghiou; A. G. Leventis Gallery. Source frame preserved; proportionally resized and JPEG compressed.
works.license: No reuse licence verified
works.description: Steps, balcony and blue openings make the house recognisable even as its walls tilt and narrow. Georghiou changes proportion without losing the building's practical parts. The empty street gives those alterations room to register. Compare the long body in *Nude with Blue Pillow*: stretching is a way of organising a familiar subject across very different kinds of picture.

works.title: Those Left Behind
works.credit: Michael Michaeledes; A. G. Leventis Gallery, AGLG 504. Source frame preserved; proportionally resized and JPEG compressed.
works.license: No reuse licence verified
works.description: The seated people face away, leaving the viewer on the same shore behind them. A distant vessel and the water separating it from the group give the title a visible structure. Their individual circumstances remain unspecified. Boats and timber occupy the near ground, while departure is held at the horizon, beyond the figures' immediate reach.

works.title: Sunrise
works.credit: Solomos Frangoulides; A. G. Leventis Gallery. Source frame preserved; proportionally resized and JPEG compressed.
works.license: No reuse licence verified
works.description: With almost no solid landmark, the distinction between sea and sky rests on slight changes of colour. The narrow reflection establishes a direction across otherwise open water. Frangoulides gives the scene enough information to locate light without filling it with objects. Its spareness makes an instructive pause before the inhabited, furnished room of *Chatting*.

works.title: Chatting
works.credit: Solomos Frangoulides; A. G. Leventis Gallery. Source frame preserved; proportionally resized and JPEG compressed.
works.license: No reuse licence verified
works.description: Furniture and household things stay close to the people, making conversation one activity within an occupied room. Turned heads and separate arm positions prevent the gathering from becoming a formal row. The dim interior provides many small points of attention. Each figure belongs to the shared setting without being required to acknowledge the others in exactly the same way.

works.title: Nude with Blue Pillow
works.credit: George Pol. Georghiou; A. G. Leventis Gallery. Source frame preserved; proportionally resized and JPEG compressed.
works.license: No reuse licence verified
works.description: The long body accommodates itself to a narrow canvas. Sparse indications of furniture leave its contour and the blue pillow carrying most of the composition. Georghiou's altered proportions remain plainly visible rather than being disguised as natural anatomy. The picture can therefore be read both as a reclining figure and as a deliberately stretched arrangement of forms.

works.title: A Walk in the Orchard
works.catalogueTitle: Promenade dans le Verger / A Walk in the Orchard
works.credit: Image source: A. G. Leventis Gallery. No item-specific reuse licence stated on museum object page
works.license: No item-specific reuse licence stated on museum object page
works.description: The walkers enter an already busy pattern of leaves and grass. Their scale and handling allow them to belong to the orchard without taking control of it. Tree trunks provide intervals through the short touches of colour. Pissarro distributes attention across the inhabited landscape, so that identifying the people is only one part of seeing the painting.

works.title: The Beach at Trouville
works.catalogueTitle: The Beach at Trouville / La Plage de Trouville
works.credit: Image source: A. G. Leventis Gallery. No item-specific reuse licence stated on museum object page
works.license: No item-specific reuse licence stated on museum object page
works.description: Boudin leaves the visitors small beneath a generous sky. Figures and buildings form a low band of activity, while the sea supplies a cooler distance behind them. Leisure belongs to the coast, but weather occupies more of the picture than any individual outing. The low horizon keeps those two scales of attention in view together.

works.title: The Outing
works.medium: Oil on board mounted on a cradled panel
works.credit: Image source: A. G. Leventis Gallery. No item-specific reuse licence stated on museum object page
works.license: No item-specific reuse licence stated on museum object page
works.description: The mirror gives another angle on a woman who appears to be preparing to leave. It also makes the furnished room less immediately simple to navigate. Figure, reflection and patches of colour interrupt one another. Bonnard preserves the partial, changing information of a passing domestic action rather than clearing the setting for an isolated portrait.

works.title: Valley with Grazing Goats, Sunrise
works.catalogueTitle: La Vallée aux Chèvres (Soleil Levant) / Valley with Grazing Goats (Sunrise)
works.credit: Image source: A. G. Leventis Gallery. No item-specific reuse licence stated on museum object page
works.license: No item-specific reuse licence stated on museum object page
works.description: Thin trees divide the valley while still allowing light to pass between them. Corot creates distance through a modest shift from darker near ground to a lighter opening beyond. Small animals and people give that distance a measure. A restricted range of greens and browns is sufficient because the arrangement of light already separates the landscape's parts.

works.title: Outing in the Bois de Boulogne
works.catalogueTitle: Promenade au Bois de Boulogne / Outing in the Bois de Boulogne
works.credit: Image source: A. G. Leventis Gallery. No item-specific reuse licence stated on museum object page
works.license: No item-specific reuse licence stated on museum object page
works.description: Blue lines identify horses and riders with surprisingly little enclosure. Scattered colour and loose branches leave much of the pale surface available around them. The openness lets movement remain more apparent than mass. Beside the detailed Venetian city view, this outing demonstrates how a public place can be established without fully describing its buildings or ground.

works.title: Regatta in the Channel
works.catalogueTitle: Régates sur la Manche / Regatta in the Channel
works.credit: Image source: A. G. Leventis Gallery. No item-specific reuse licence stated on museum object page
works.license: No item-specific reuse licence stated on museum object page
works.description: Sails repeat as coloured triangles above the curves of hulls and waves. Their close overlap leaves little deep water between the boats, so outlines and strong colour must keep them distinct. Dufy makes the regatta busy at the level of the surface itself. Compare its density with the broad breathing space above Boudin's beach.

works.title: Aline Asking for Alms
works.catalogueTitle: Aline Demande l’Aumône / Aline Asking for Alms
works.medium: Black chalk and brown wash on laid paper
works.credit: Image source: A. G. Leventis Gallery. No item-specific reuse licence stated on museum object page
works.license: No item-specific reuse licence stated on museum object page
works.description: A bent back and reaching hands do most of the narrative work. The lightly indicated arch locates the exchange without demanding a fully furnished environment. Unworked paper remains around the figures, making their approach easier to follow. The drawing shows how an encounter can become readable through the direction of bodies before the setting is extensively developed.

works.title: The Piazzetta, Venice, with the Campanile under Repair
works.catalogueTitle: The Piazzetta, Venice, with the Campanile under Repair
works.credit: Image source: A. G. Leventis Gallery. No item-specific reuse licence stated on museum object page
works.license: No item-specific reuse licence stated on museum object page
works.description: The repair named in the title prevents the landmark from being simply timeless scenery. Below it, small figures move across paving organised by the receding façades. They measure the buildings' height as well as inhabiting the square. Architecture dominates the composition, but its particular condition makes the view a record of a city being maintained.

works.title: Virgin of the Immaculate Conception
works.medium: Pen and brown ink with brown wash on brown-toned paper
works.credit: Image source: A. G. Leventis Gallery. No item-specific reuse licence stated on museum object page
works.license: No item-specific reuse licence stated on museum object page
works.description: The Virgin's raised position and the angels beneath establish the image before much surrounding detail is supplied. Pale washes and lines give the falling drapery a direction within the light paper. The subject needs a hierarchy of bodies more than a fully enclosed location. What remains open helps make that upward arrangement legible.

works.title: Young Drinker
works.credit: Image source: A. G. Leventis Gallery. © A. G. Leventis Gallery
works.license: © A. G. Leventis Gallery
works.description: The jug is large enough to change the boy's balance. His head tips back and his elbows rise, while the shoes remain firmly planted below. Pantazis makes weight visible through adjustment rather than through a written description of the vessel. The spare warm background leaves the complete chain of effort, from feet to hands, easy to follow.

closingSections.title: Try a dense picture beside a spare one
paragraphs: Pair *Trellises and Shadows* with *Sunrise*, or the regatta with Trouville. Ask which few decisions allow each image to hold together. The selection is a reading guide rather than a guaranteed installation plan; check the gallery's current information before organising a visit around one work.
